checks: Checked original f5833eb86e30876b §§1–3 for the pyramid inequality, the three-edge optimization and the application to the proper-A, zero-B circuit. The frozen source digest matches.

Each pyramid base lies on an actual facet and its apex lies in the convex body, so the pyramid lies in the body. For an interior apex, the rays from it partition the enclosing simplex by first boundary facet up to ridge cones of zero volume. For a boundary apex the bound also follows by taking apexes inside B tending to the given point and passing to the continuous barycentric coefficients. The relative volume factor is precisely the facet area ratio times the barycentric altitude ratio.

Positive a_i make every actual edge trace a nonempty positive-length interval. The polygon obtained from all endpoints follows their cyclic order, leaving exactly the three corner regions up to null boundaries. The area of a corner triangle relative to the reference is the product of its two adjacent edge fractions, since the determinant scales separately along those two edges.

Each omitted-area expression is affine in a single edge split when the other two are fixed. Pushing to endpoints in sequence does not reduce the sum. At endpoint allocations no two corners can both receive both edges, as any two corners share an edge. Thus the largest omitted area is bounded by the product of the two largest omissions, which are bounded by the two largest 1-a_i. An exact rational enumeration of endpoint allocations also checked this identity. A cut at the vertex shared by those two edges attains equality, and the whole triangle handles zero product.

The actual critical circuit has the required fixed-mark local minimizing hypothesis, rank and positive balance and zero B capture. Each proper A trace has positive section area, and its parallel B supporting section has at least that area by the predecessor. The common normalized B simplex contains B, so its corresponding facet fractions dominate the stated a_i. The planar formula needs all three a_i positive and its geometric sharpness does not establish sharpness in the restricted mixed circuit class.
